description:
# Outcome

Deliver a Jidoka-first implementation path for `jido_cli`. The backlog has 33 atomic stories in six phases. It preserves the existing automation boundary and puts runtime substance in Jidoka.

# Product boundaries

- `jido_cli` owns arguments, files, scenarios, suites, matrices, concurrency, JSONL, terminal presentation, exit status, and artifacts.
- Jidoka owns turns, ordered session state, effects, reviews, cancellation, persistence, recovery, execution environments, extensions, and session sequencing.
- Agent, scenario, and suite files stay data-only.
- One matrix cell gets one fresh Jidoka session.
- `jido.case-result` stays the external automation boundary. stdout is JSONL and diagnostics use stderr.
- No story adds `jido_eval`, `jido compare`, or `jido validate`.
- LitterBox stays outside the CLI and Jidoka core.

# Ranked dependency map

flowchart TD

  B2 --> S4["tqg.2.4 Headless cancellation"]
  S1 --> S4
  S3 --> S4
  B1 --> E1["tqg.3.1 Policy gate"] --> E2["tqg.3.2 Portable execution data"] --> E3["tqg.3.3 Trusted profiles"] --> E4["tqg.3.4 Lifecycle manager"] --> E5["tqg.3.5 Durable bindings"]
  E3 --> E6["tqg.3.6 Profile selection"]

  B1 --> X1["tqg.4.1 Extension requests"] --> X2["tqg.4.2 Trusted identity"] --> X3["tqg.4.3 Lifecycle events"] --> X4["tqg.4.4 Built-in host"]

# Ready rule

The only dependency-root implementation story is `jido_cli-tqg.1.1`. Beadwork shows this main epic first while it is open. Per the request, no issue is started or closed.
